§1.3 Atomic Orbitals

1.3 Atomic Orbitals

Eigenfunctions from (1.2.1)(1.2.1)(1.2.1) gives wave function for a given nucleus to be described by three quantum numbers.

The principal quantum number 𝑛 is a positive integer that determines the binding energy of an electron assuming single electron (1.2.2)(1.2.2)(1.2.2). In this case of multiple electrons, there may be a correction term due to electron repulsion that is relatively small compared to the term given by (1.2.2). Hence, categorize all electrons in an atom by this number gives the shell of the electron.

The orbital angular momentum quantum number ℓ takes value from ℓ=0,1,2,…,𝑛−1. It determines the angular-momentum magnitude and the subshell or orbital shape.

The magnetic quantum number 𝑚 (or 𝑚ℓ) takes values from 𝑚=−ℓ,−ℓ+1,…,ℓ−1,ℓ. It determines 𝐿𝑧=𝑚ℏ and labels a particular orbital within a subshell.

The wave function is then given by

Ψ𝑛ℓ𝑚(𝑟,𝜃,𝜑).

An orbital is given the three defining quantum number mentioned above, denote it with a number concatenated by 𝑛ℓ𝑚ℓ‾.
